tools.name: list_jurisdictions
tools.description:
List every country and state in the authenticated subscription's Lawstronaut legal corpus (name, iso, type, documents_count) — not the global unfiltered catalog, and not legal documents or full text.

When to use: Call FIRST, before any jurisdiction-scoped legal query, so you know which iso codes are valid for this credential. When not: Skip if you already have this list from earlier in the session. Do not use this to fetch documents, markdown, source files, or portals.

Parameters: Takes none — invoke with {}. Do not pass iso, country, limit, offset, or other filters; they are not accepted and would not change the result. There is no page size or default filter. Empty data means the subscription includes no jurisdictions.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription and portal data.

Returns: A list of jurisdictions matching the filters, with pagination information.

inputSchema.description: No arguments. Call with {}. Scope comes from the authenticated subscription, not from caller-supplied filters.

iso.description: Canonical ISO code to pass to later tools, e.g. BE

type.description: country for national, state for sub-national

documents_count.description: Number of documents in the jurisdiction

data.description: Full subscribed list, countries then states; empty if the subscription has no jurisdictions.

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description:
Lists the top-level legal domains (id, domain_id, domain name). This is the first taxonomy step. It does not return subdomains, categories, documents, or jurisdictions.

When to use: When you need the domain list or a name match. Examples: 'what legal domains exist?', 'find the domain for private law'. Pass domain only to narrow by name. When not: Do not use this for children of a domain. For subdomains use list_subdomains with the returned domain_id. For categories use list_categories. For subcategories use list_subcategories. For law types use list_law_types. For documents use list_documents or search. For jurisdictions use list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this domain list for the same domain filter.

Parameters: domain is an optional case-insensitive substring of the domain name. There is no parent id and no iso. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. next_id is the numeric id from the previous pagination.next_id; omit it on the first page. A null next_id means there is no further page. Empty data means no domain name matched.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads the current domain table. total_count is the full match count, not the page size. Results are not limited to a jurisdiction.

Returns: A page of {id, domain_id, domain}. Example: {"id":1,"domain_id":"A","domain":"Private law"}. Pass domain_id, not id, to list_subdomains.

next_id.description: Next ID to paginate the results
Numeric id cursor for the next page, or null when there is no next page

id.description: Numeric row id. Use only as pagination.next_id, not as domain_id.

domain_id.description: Domain reference, such as A. Pass this to list_subdomains as domain_id.

domain.description: Domain display name, or null when unset

data.description: Top-level domains; empty if none match. Not limited to a jurisdiction.

tools.name: list_subdomains
tools.description:
Lists subdomains under one domain (id, domain_id, subdomain_id, subdomain name). This is the second taxonomy step.

When to use: When you already have a domain_id from list_domains. Examples: 'subdomains under domain A', 'international law under Private law'. Pass subdomain only to narrow by name. When not: Do not call without a domain_id from list_domains; use list_domains first. For categories under a subdomain use list_categories with subdomain_id. For subcategories use list_subcategories. For law types use list_law_types. For documents use list_documents or search. Skip if you already have this subdomain list for the same domain_id and subdomain filter.

Parameters: domain_id (required) is the domain reference from list_domains, such as A, and is uppercased before the query. It is not the numeric id. subdomain is an optional case-insensitive substring of the subdomain name. An unknown domain_id returns Domain not found. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. next_id is the numeric id from pagination.next_id, not subdomain_id. Empty data means that domain has no matching subdomain.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads the current subdomain table. total_count is the full match count, not the page size.

Returns: A page of {id, domain_id, subdomain_id, subdomain}. Example: {"id":1,"domain_id":"A","subdomain_id":"A.1","subdomain":"Private International Law"}. Pass subdomain_id, not id, to list_categories.

next_id.description: Next ID to paginate the results
Cursor ID for the next page, or null when there is no next page

domain_id.description: Parent domain reference, such as A

subdomain_id.description: Subdomain reference, such as A.1. Pass this to list_categories as subdomain_id.

subdomain.description: Subdomain display name, or null when unset

data.description: Subdomains in the requested domain that have data; empty if none match.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description:
Lists categories under one subdomain, with the parent domain and subdomain names. This is the third taxonomy step.

When to use: When you already have a subdomain_id from list_subdomains. Examples: 'categories under subdomain A.1', 'find a category named jurisdiction'. Pass category_name only to narrow by name. When not: Do not use this for subcategories; use list_subcategories with the returned category_id. Do not use it for law types; use list_law_types. For the parent lists use list_domains and list_subdomains. For documents use list_documents or search. Do not call without a subdomain_id from list_subdomains. Skip if you already have this category list for the same subdomain_id and category_name.

Parameters: subdomain_id is the subdomain reference from list_subdomains, such as A.1. A call without it, or with an unknown value, returns Subdomain not found. category_name is an optional case-insensitive substring of the category name; the parameter is category_name, not category. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. next_id is the numeric id from pagination.next_id, not category_id. Empty data means that subdomain has no matching category.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads the current category table. total_count is the full match count, not the page size. The input marks subdomain_id optional, but the query returns Subdomain not found when it is missing.

Returns: A page of {id, domain, subdomain, category_id, category_name}. domain and subdomain are display names, not reference codes. Example category_id "A.1.1", category_name "General Private International Law". Pass category_id, not id, to list_subcategories.

category_name.description: Category display name, or null when unset

tools.name: list_subcategories
tools.description:
Lists subcategories under one category (id, category_id, category_name, subcategory_id, subcategory_name). This is the fourth taxonomy step.

When to use: When you already have a category_id from list_categories. Examples: 'subcategories of category A.1.1', 'find the Jurisdiction subcategory'. Pass subcategory_name only to narrow by name. When not: Do not use this for law types; use list_law_types with the returned subcategory_id. For categories use list_categories. For domains or subdomains use list_domains or list_subdomains. For documents use list_documents or search. Do not call without a category_id from list_categories. Skip if you already have this subcategory list for the same category_id and subcategory_name.

Parameters: category_id (required) is the category reference from list_categories. It must be exactly three dot-separated segments ending in a number, such as A.1.1, and is uppercased before the query. subcategory_name is an optional case-insensitive substring of the subcategory name; the parameter is subcategory_name, not subcategory. An unknown category_id returns Category not found. A category_id with the wrong shape is rejected before the query. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. next_id is the numeric id from pagination.next_id, not subcategory_id. Empty data means that category has no matching subcategory.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads the current subcategory table. total_count is the full match count, not the page size.

Returns: A page of {id, category_id, category_name, subcategory_id, subcategory_name}. Example: {"category_id":"A.1.1","category_name":"General Private International Law","subcategory_id":"A.1.1.1","subcategory_name":"Jurisdiction"}. Pass subcategory_id, not id, to list_law_types.

tools.name: list_law_types
tools.description:
Lists law types under one subcategory, with the parent category and subcategory names. This is the last taxonomy step. It does not return documents.

When to use: When you already have a subcategory_id from list_subcategories. Examples: 'law types under subcategory A.1.1.1', 'find law types named statute'. Pass law_type only to narrow by name. When not: Do not use this to list subcategories, categories, domains, or documents. For those use list_subcategories, list_categories, list_domains, list_documents, or search. Do not call without a subcategory_id from list_subcategories. Skip if you already have this law type list for the same subcategory_id and law_type filter.

Parameters: subcategory_id (required) is the subcategory reference from list_subcategories. It must be exactly four dot-separated segments, such as A.1.1.1, and is uppercased before the query. law_type is an optional case-insensitive substring of the law type name. A subcategory_id with the wrong shape is rejected before the query. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. next_id is the numeric id from pagination.next_id, not subcategory_id. Empty data means that subcategory has no matching law type.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads the current law type table. total_count is the full match count, not the page size. There is no further taxonomy tool after this one.

Returns: A page of {id, category_id, category_name, subcategory_id, subcategory_name, law_type_id, law_type}. id and law_type_id are the same numeric id. Example law_type "Statute".

tools.name: list_portals
tools.description:
Lists the source portals available through this tool, with metadata such as jurisdiction and language. A jurisdiction may have multiple portals, including those maintained by regulators or ministries.

When to use: When you need portals, legal websites, or sources for a known iso. Pass optional name, tag, or lang only to narrow that list. When not: Do not use this to read a document. For metadata use list_documents. For plain text use list_full_text. For structured Markdown use list_markdown. For a complete citation bundle use evidence_pull. For a temporary source-file URL use document_presigned_url. Do not call without an iso from list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this portal list for the same iso and filters.

Parameters: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions (e.g. BE, or US_CA for a state). name, tag, and lang are optional and combined with AND: name is a case-insensitive substring of the portal name, tag must match one portal tag exactly, lang must match the language name exactly (e.g. English). With limit, next_id parameters to paginate the results. Empty data means the iso is outside the subscription, or no portal with crawled links matched.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription and portal data. Portals with total_links of 0 are omitted.

Returns: A list of portals matching the filters, with pagination information.

iso.description: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions (e.g. BE, or US_CA for a state).

name.description: Case-insensitive substring of the portal name

portal_tags.description: Exact portal tag; the portal must include this tag

next_id.description: Next portal ID to return

inputSchema.description: iso is required. name, tag, and lang are optional AND filters. Scope is the authenticated subscription.

next_id.description: Cursor ID for the next page, or null when there is no next page

name.description: Portal name in the source language

name_en.description: English name, or null when the portal has none

state.description: State or region name; empty string when the portal is national

portal_tags.description: Tags on the portal; null when none are set

documents_count.description: Number of documents in the portal

data.description: Portals in the requested jurisdiction that have crawled links; empty if none match.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description:
Lists document metadata in a jurisdiction (title, dates, source, classification) with filters and pagination. It does not return the document body, a citation bundle, or a source-file URL.

When to use: When you need to find or browse documents before reading them. Example: 'which Belgian employment statutes mention night work?' Use the returned uuid with a body or citation tool. When not: Do not use this for the body or the file. For plain text, use list_full_text (example: 'quote the operative wording'). For structured Markdown, use list_markdown (example: 'keep the article headings'). For a complete citation bundle — metadata, permanent legal link, citation template, body, and a temporary source-file URL — use evidence_pull (example: 'show me the source'). For only a temporary URL to the original file, use document_presigned_url (example: 'download the PDF'). Do not call without an iso from list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this document list for the same iso and filters.

Parameters: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions (e.g. BE, or US_CA for a state). version, section_title, date_of_decision, file_data_only, issuing_authority, type_of_authority, source_identifier, source_secondary_identifier, tag are optional, section_title is a case-insensitive substring of the section title, date_of_decision is a date, file_data_only is a boolean, issuing_authority is a case-insensitive substring of the issuing authority, type_of_authority is a case-insensitive substring of the type of authority, source_identifier is a case-insensitive substring of the source identifier, source_secondary_identifier is a case-insensitive substring of the source secondary identifier, tag is a case-insensitive substring of the tag. With limit, next_id parameters to paginate the results. Empty data means the iso is outside the subscription, or no document matched.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription and document data. Documents with total_links of 0 are omitted.

Returns: A list of documents matching the filters, with pagination information.

tools.name: list_full_text
tools.description:
Returns the plain-text body of documents (id, uuid, version, text). This is the plain-text read: wording only, with no Markdown headings or lists, and no citation metadata.

When to use: When you need the body as plain text. Examples: 'quote the operative wording of this Belgian statute', 'give me the raw text of uuid …'. Pass uuid when you already have one document; otherwise filter by title and paginate. When not: For structured Markdown that keeps headings and lists, use list_markdown. For a complete citation bundle in one call — metadata, permanent legal link, citation template, body, and a temporary source-file URL — use evidence_pull (example: 'show me the source'). For only a temporary URL to the original PDF or source file, use document_presigned_url (example: 'download the original file'). To browse titles and dates without the body, use list_documents or search. For one historical version's metadata plus both bodies, use document_version. Do not call without an iso from list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this plain text for the same iso, uuid, and filters.

Parameters: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions and is uppercased before the query (e.g. BE, or US_CA for a state). uuid is optional; when set, the call targets that document. title is an optional case-insensitive substring. with_empty_data defaults to false and omits documents that have no stored plain text; true includes them with text null. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. include_total adds pagination.total_count when true. Other optional filters match the input schema and are combined with AND.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT plus a read of the stored text. Does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription data and the stored plain text. An archived uuid returns an archived error instead of the body.

Returns: A page of {id, uuid, version, text} where text is plain text. Empty data means nothing matched, or the iso is outside the subscription.

tools.name: list_markdown
tools.description:
Returns the structured Markdown body of documents (id, uuid, version, markdown). Headings and lists stay intact. This is not plain text, not a citation bundle, and not a file URL.

When to use: When you need the body as structured Markdown. Examples: 'show this regulation with its article headings', 'give me Markdown I can render for uuid …'. Pass uuid when you already have one document; otherwise filter by title and paginate. When not: For plain text with no Markdown structure, use list_full_text (example: 'quote the operative wording'). For a complete citation bundle in one call — metadata, permanent legal link, citation template, body, and a temporary source-file URL — use evidence_pull (example: 'show me the source'). For only a temporary URL to the original PDF or source file, use document_presigned_url (example: 'download the original file'). To browse titles and dates without the body, use list_documents or search. For one historical version's metadata plus both bodies, use document_version. Do not call without an iso from list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this Markdown for the same iso, uuid, and filters.

Parameters: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions and is uppercased before the query (e.g. BE, or US_CA for a state). uuid is optional; when set, the call targets that document. title is an optional case-insensitive substring. with_empty_data defaults to false and omits documents that have no stored Markdown; true includes them with markdown null. limit defaults to 20 and is capped at 100. include_total adds pagination.total_count when true. Other optional filters match the input schema and are combined with AND.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT plus a read of the stored Markdown. Does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription data and the stored Markdown. An archived uuid returns an archived error instead of the body.

Returns: A page of {id, uuid, version, markdown} where markdown is structured Markdown. Empty data means nothing matched, or the iso is outside the subscription.

tools.name: document_presigned_url
tools.description:
Returns a temporary signed URL to the original source file (PDF or other stored file) for one document. The URL expires. This tool does not return the document body or a citation bundle.

When to use: When you need to open or download the original file. Examples: 'give me the PDF for uuid …', 'link to the source file so I can download it'. Use the uuid from list_documents, search, or horizon_scan. When not: For plain text of the body, use list_full_text (example: 'quote the operative wording'). For structured Markdown, use list_markdown (example: 'keep the article headings'). For a complete citation bundle — metadata, permanent legal link, citation template, body, and this temporary URL together — use evidence_pull (example: 'show me the source'). For a permanent citation link without a file download, use the legal_link from evidence_pull or list_documents. Do not call without a uuid. Skip if you already have an unexpired URL for that uuid.

Parameters: uuid (required) is the document UUID. There is no iso parameter. The response includes expires_at; fetch the URL before it expires. A missing file or an archived document returns an error rather than a URL.

Behavior: Read-only. Looks up the stored file and signs a temporary URL. Does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached. Each call signs a new URL. expires_at is when that URL stops working. The URL is not a permanent legal link.

Returns: One object: uuid, url (temporary source-file URL), and expires_at. url is empty when no file could be signed.

url.description: Temporary signed URL to the original source file. Fetch it before expires_at. Not the document body.

expires_at.description: ISO timestamp when the temporary URL stops working

data.description: Presigned URL for the requested document

tools.name: document_version
tools.description:
Retrieves a specific document with a specific version

When to use: The user wants to find a specific document with a specific version When not: The user wants to find a specific document with a specific version but the document is not found

Parameters: uuid (required) is the UUID of the document, version (required) is the version of the document

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription and document data. Documents with total_links of 0 are omitted.

Returns: A document with the specific version

file.description: File data, or null when the document has no file

tools.name: horizon_scan
tools.description:
Scans recent legal documents across jurisdictions.

When to use: When you need to find legal content for a specific jurisdiction and optional filters. When not: Do not use this to read a document body or download a file. For plain text use list_full_text. For structured Markdown use list_markdown. For a complete citation bundle use evidence_pull. For a temporary source-file URL use document_presigned_url. Do not call without an iso from list_jurisdictions. Skip if you already have this scan for the same iso and filters.

Parameters: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions (e.g. BE, or US_CA for a state). issuing_authority, type_of_authority. Topic, since, date_field, status, include_repealed, max_per_jurisdiction are optional. Empty data means the iso is outside the subscription, or no document matched.

Behavior: Read-only SELECT; does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. The only effect is a database read. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached; each call reads current subscription and document data. Documents with total_links of 0 are omitted.

Returns: A list of documents matching the filters, with pagination information.

topic.description: Optional filter (matches title) e.g. "employee monitoring" or "workplace surveillance"

date_field.description: Which date to window on. "crawling_date" (default) = when Lawstronaut crawled it. "publication_date" = when officially published. "last_updated" = when corpus record last changed.

status.description: Optional filter on status field e.g. "new", "updated" String.

type_of_authority.description: Optional filter on type of authority

include_repealed.description: If false, drop documents where repealed=true

max_per_jurisdiction.description: Max docs to return per jurisdiction (1-100)

next_id.description: Cursor ID for the next page, or null when there is no next page

issuing_authority_tags.description: Issuing Authority Tags of the content

text.description: Path hint for the plain-text body. Call list_full_text to read it; this field is not the text.

markdown.description: Path hint for the structured Markdown body. Call list_markdown to read it; this field is not the Markdown.

url.description: Source-file metadata, not a downloadable URL. Call document_presigned_url for a temporary source-file URL.

file.description: File metadata, or null when the document has no file. Not a citation bundle; call evidence_pull for that.

crawled_at.description: Date and time the content was crawled

source_updated_at.description: Date and time the source was updated

data.description: Documents in the requested jurisdiction that have crawled links; empty if none match. Each item is a content item.

tools.name: evidence_pull
tools.description:
Returns one complete citation bundle for a single document: metadata, a permanent legal_link, a citation_template, the body, and a temporary source-file URL when one exists.

When to use: When one call must support a citation or an audit. Examples: 'show me the source for this Irish statute', 'cite uuid … with its authority, date, link, and text'. Prefer this over calling the body and file tools separately. When not: For plain text alone, use list_full_text (example: 'quote the operative wording'). For structured Markdown alone, use list_markdown (example: 'keep the article headings'). For only a temporary URL to the original PDF or source file, use document_presigned_url (example: 'download the original file'). To browse or search without the bundle, use list_documents, search, or horizon_scan. For one historical version, use document_version. Do not call without an iso from list_jurisdictions and the document uuid. Skip if you already have this bundle for the same iso and uuid.

Parameters: iso (required) is a jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions and is uppercased (e.g. IE, NL, US_CA). uuid (required) is the document UUID from list_documents, search, or horizon_scan. include_text defaults to true and fetches the body. include_source_url defaults to true and adds a temporary signed URL to the original file when one exists. text_format defaults to 'markdown' (structured Markdown); 'plain' returns plain text instead. Set include_text or include_source_url to false only when that part of the bundle is unnecessary.

Behavior: Read-only. Reads the document record, optionally the stored body, and optionally signs a temporary source-file URL. Does not create, update, or delete records, files, or credentials. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Not cached. The source-file URL is temporary: source_file_note says to fetch it promptly, and legal_link is the permanent citation URL. source_file_url is null when no original file is stored. An archived document returns an archived error.

Returns: One citation bundle: uuid, version, metadata, legal_link, citation_template, and, when requested, content_format plus content, and source_file_url.

iso.description: Document's jurisdiction ISO code, e.g. 'IE', 'NL', 'US', etc.

include_source_url.description: Fetch a temporary signed URL to the original file (PDF etc.) where available (default True).

issuing_authority_tags.description: Issuing Authority Tags of the content

markdown.description: Path hint for the structured Markdown body. Call list_markdown to read it; this field is not the Markdown.

url.description: Source-file metadata, not a downloadable URL. Call document_presigned_url for a temporary source-file URL.

file.description: File metadata, or null when the document has no file. Not a citation bundle; call evidence_pull for that.

source_updated_at.description: Date and time the source was updated

content.description: Document body in content_format: structured Markdown or plain text

source_file_url.description: Temporary signed URL to the original source file, or null when none exists. Permanent citation URL is legal_link.

data.description: Citation chain for the requested document: metadata, legal link, optional source file URL, and optional body.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Searches legal documents using OpenSearch to discover relevant documents based on the supplied search criteria. Returns matching documents and their available metadata.

When to use: Use when you need to discover relevant legal documents through search, especially when looking for documents matching a search query rather than retrieving a structured list. Use this to explore legal content relevant to a topic, legal issue, phrase, or other supported search criteria. When not: Do not use this to browse with structured filters and cursor pagination; use list_documents. Do not use it to read a body or a file. For plain text use list_full_text (example: 'quote the operative wording'). For structured Markdown use list_markdown (example: 'keep the article headings'). For a complete citation bundle use evidence_pull (example: 'show me the source'). For a temporary source-file URL use document_presigned_url (example: 'download the PDF'). For one historical version use document_version. Do not call without a valid iso from list_jurisdictions. Avoid repeating an equivalent search when you already have sufficient results for the same query and filters.

Parameters: iso (required) is the jurisdiction code from list_jurisdictions (e.g. BE or US_CA for a state). Provide the search query and any supported optional filters defined by the input schema. Optional filters may narrow the search by document metadata, dates, authority, source identifiers, tags, or other supported criteria. Use only parameters defined by the schema. The results depend on the query, jurisdiction, filters, and the user's subscription access. An empty data array means no matching documents were returned; it does not necessarily mean that the jurisdiction has no documents.

Behavior: Read-only search operation. Does not create, update, or delete documents, records, files, or credentials. The primary side effect is the computational and resource cost of executing an OpenSearch query. Auth: tools/call requires OAuth 2.0 or a Bearer token (401 if missing, invalid, revoked, or no active subscription). Rate limits: none at the MCP layer; safe to retry. Search results are determined by the OpenSearch query implementation, relevance logic, supported filters, and available indexed data. Results may not include every document in the jurisdiction. Search results may differ from list_documents because the tools use different retrieval mechanisms. Repeating a search executes another query. Do not assume results are cached or that the search index contains every recently updated document.

Returns: Matching legal documents and their available metadata, together with a result message. The returned documents depend on the search query, jurisdiction, supported filters, and subscription permissions.
